PullRequest.Title: mcp: enforce URL policy after variable resolution
PullRequest.Body:
MCP URL rules must be enforced against the fully resolved launch, even if the resulting URL still contains text that resembles a configuration variable. Policy updates must also recheck existing connections and keep blocked servers from exposing cached tools or prompts.

- Separate preliminary definition checks from authoritative runtime URL allow/deny checks. Defer only URL/command rules whose fields contain syntactically complete configuration variables, using a shared linear-time detector that preserves the configuration resolver's balanced/nested-variable syntax.
- Recheck the local resolved connection immediately before starting its transport, even when reactive policy enforcement has already cleared the stored connection.
- Re-evaluate policy changes and stop connections that become blocked. Retain the last resolved identity after disposal while the server definition remains unchanged, so the block and cached-metadata suppression remain effective. Invalidate that identity on the first non-equivalent definition change, so reverting a definition cannot resurrect a stale destination.
- Allow interactive retries to re-resolve edited or reset inputs while keeping cached metadata hidden until the new resolved identity passes policy. Cancellation and repeat denial retain the block; quiet starts do not bypass it. Access and name restrictions are checked before provider activation or input/command resolution, for both initial starts and retries.
- Settle pending startup on explicit stop or disposal, allowing a retry after policy restoration without regressing normal transport restarts. Do not start a disposed connection.
- Cover resolved allow/deny enforcement, permitted variable-based definitions, literal incomplete markers, access/name restrictions, cached metadata, definition changes, and policy revocation during both running and starting states. Include input edit/reset recovery, cancelled and repeatedly denied retries, and repeated-incomplete-marker performance regressions.

RegressionFixes.Mechanism: Pending start promises waited exclusively for Running/Error while explicit disposal transitioned the connection to Stopped, so callers and the per-server sequencer could remain blocked indefinitely after policy-driven or user-driven cleanup.
RegressionFixes.Symptom: Stopping or disposing an MCP connection during Starting could leave startup and later sequenced operations waiting forever.
RegressionFixes.FixedBehavior: The connection now records an explicit stop request and line 156 makes pending state waiters accept Stopped when that request is active, so disposing or stopping a Starting transport releases all queued startup callers instead of retaining an indefinitely blocked critical path.
RegressionFixes.Evidence: In the base revision, start() callers that arrived while a connection was Starting waited only for Running or Error via _waitForState. dispose() then forced the state to Stopped, which was outside those accepted kinds, leaving every pending start promise unresolved; the added tests exercise two concurrent starts and prove both previously vulnerable waiters now settle on stop/dispose. Blame attributes the old wait condition at base line 141 to eb700003ebf3797af1de1f9e222478d6d7f7eea3.

Scenarios.Scenario: Discovering MCP server definitions and computing their at-rest policy state
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Registry publication synchronously reaches each McpServer policy derived value when observed; policy reads and variable detection must complete before the server's displayed state and cached metadata are exposed. No subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, or network boundary is reached.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Work scales with the number of discovered servers, each URL/command length, and configured allow/deny matcher count. The new detector is linear in the URL/command text and short-circuits command arguments after the first complete variable.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Policy derivations run synchronously per observed server; there is no asynchronous boundary or parallel work in discovery policy evaluation.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Configuration values are in-memory; policy matchers are filtered per evaluation rather than cached. The retained resolved identity is one entry per McpServer and is invalidated on the first non-equivalent definition change. Cached tools/prompts remain hidden while blocked.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed detector, matcher calls, observable dependencies, and per-server ownership are directly visible in the changed code and matcher implementation.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Installations with exceptionally many servers or unusually large policy arrays are possible, but normal definitions are small and policy-change frequency is low.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The new at-rest checks add bounded linear CPU work and replace a broader marker test with a linear balanced-variable detector; the 64 KiB repeated-marker tests specifically cover the adversarial shape.

Scenarios.Scenario: Starting or interactively retrying a server whose definition contains configuration variables
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The per-server Sequencer runs preliminary policy evaluation, optional extension activation, connection resolution (trust, provider launch resolution, variable/input resolution, storage update, and optional sandbox transformation), authoritative resolved policy evaluation, and only then transport startup. The resolved policy check completes before delegate.start creates a subprocess or network transport.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Activate the owning extension and await delegate provider initialization when a lazy extension-backed server has not activated.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one activation sequence for a start after the activation-event completion check; subsequent starts use the completed activation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same activation path preceded connection resolution before the PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks connection resolution and startup only for an unactivated extension-backed collection.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read/update saved configuration inputs and resolve launch variables during McpRegistry.resolveConnection.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One resolution pipeline per actual start attempt; quiet retries blocked by retained policy perform zero resolutions, while an explicit interactive retry performs one.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Variable-bearing starts already resolved inputs through the same registry pipeline; the diff preserves one pipeline for an allowed interactive retry and prevents it for access/name-denied or quiet retries.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must finish before authoritative policy evaluation and transport startup.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Transform a local launch for sandboxing when enabled.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most once per resolved local start attempt; only for sandbox-enabled definitions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Sandbox transformation was already part of every applicable resolveConnection call.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Completes before the authoritative policy check; a URL/command policy denial after resolution can therefore include pre-existing resolution/sandbox setup but does not launch the MCP transport.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Start a local stdio MCP transport via the selected host delegate.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Zero for definitions blocked preliminarily or resolved identities blocked authoritatively; one for an allowed start attempt.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Allowed starts invoked one delegate transport start. The diff adds the authoritative check before this boundary, reducing blocked launches to zero.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Starts the server process and then startup waits for Running/Error.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Start an HTTP MCP transport via the selected host delegate.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Zero for policy-blocked identities and one for each allowed start attempt.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Allowed starts invoked one transport start; the new resolved check prevents transport creation for newly detected blocked destinations.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Establishes the MCP connection and startup waits for Running/Error.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Multiplicity is user start attempts per server. A Sequencer serializes attempts for the same server; separate servers remain independent. Interactive retry only bypasses a retained block when the current definition still has a complete configuration variable and preliminary access/name policy permits resolution.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Starts are serialized per McpServer by one Sequencer. There is no new aggregate limiter across different servers, but this diff does not add multi-server fan-out or increase allowed-start cardinality.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The last resolved identity is retained while the definition is equivalent, including after connection disposal. Quiet starts reuse the block without resolution; an explicit interactive retry may re-resolve edited/reset input. Cancellation and repeated denial retain the negative policy state; a changed definition invalidates it.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: start, resolveConnection, policy evaluation, and transport creation were traced end to end, and tests assert resolution and transport counts for quiet, interactive, cancelled, allowed, and denied retries.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Actual variable-resolution and extension-activation duration depends on provider and user interaction, but the changed branch cardinality and placement before transport launch are established.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The new retained-block retry logic does not add repeated transport starts, and the only permitted re-resolution is the explicit interactive attempt needed to observe changed inputs.

Scenarios.Scenario: Changing MCP allow/deny/access policy while servers are running or starting
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A configuration event synchronously signals each observed server policy derivation. A newly blocked server clears its disposable connection immediately; a Starting caller then settles through the new explicit-stop state, and a Running transport is disposed/stopped.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Dispose/stop each newly blocked local stdio MCP transport.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one transport cleanup per currently connected local server newly blocked by the policy event.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The prior undefined-valued observable did not invalidate after its initial value, so subsequent policy events could leave existing connections running.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cleanup is initiated synchronously from policy enforcement; transport-specific disposal may perform process shutdown work.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Dispose/stop each newly blocked HTTP MCP transport.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one transport cleanup per currently connected remote server newly blocked by the event.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Subsequent policy events were not reliably propagated by the previous constant-valued observable.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Connection teardown begins synchronously during policy handling; no new network connection is created.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Policy evaluation scales with total observed servers and matcher count; cleanup scales only with the subset of active servers that become blocked. Each server owns at most one connection.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The policy event fans out synchronously across server observers. Individual connections are disposed independently; there is no explicit global limiter, but cardinality is bounded by active MCP servers and the event is an infrequent administrative configuration change.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Resolved identities let policy remain authoritative after disposal, preventing cached metadata from reappearing. Policy relaxation recomputes from in-memory state; unchanged definitions retain identity, while changed definitions clear it.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: observable signal semantics, autorun disposal, disposable connection ownership, and transport teardown were inspected directly.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The number and shutdown cost of concurrently active MCP servers varies, but typical active-server counts are small and immediate revocation is an intentional enforcement requirement.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Although the diff activates per-connected-server teardown on revocation, this is bounded by active connections, triggered by rare policy edits, and necessary to stop disallowed external resources promptly.

Scenarios.Scenario: Stopping or disposing a connection while startup is pending
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Pending start calls wait on connection state while the per-server Sequencer cannot progress until the active start settles. Explicit stop/disposal now marks stop requested and allows Stopped to resolve those waiters.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Stop/dispose the underlying local transport when present.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One cleanup for the connection; all concurrent start callers share the same connection state and are released without duplicate transport cleanup.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Transport cleanup already occurred, but waiters accepted only Running/Error and could remain unresolved after disposal forced Stopped.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cleanup unblocks pending startup and subsequent sequenced operations.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Stop/dispose the underlying remote transport when present.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One cleanup for the connection regardless of the number of pending start callers.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The transport was disposed but pending starts could remain blocked indefinitely.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Releases the connection and now also releases pending startup promises.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The old retained-wait cost grew with concurrent callers waiting on the same Starting connection and with the lifetime of the process. The fix resolves all observers on the same state transition.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Concurrent start callers coalesce on the same state wait; outer McpServer starts are serialized by Sequencer. Stop/dispose releases all waiters without spawning replacement work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache participates. The stop-request flag is reset transactionally on a new valid start and retained only for the connection object's lifetime.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high: the base wait predicate, disposal transition, new stop flag, tests with two pending starts, and introducing commit were all established.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: How often users revoke policy or stop during Starting is unknown, but the indefinite-wait mechanism is deterministic once triggered.
Scenarios.Verdict: This PR fixes, rather than introduces, a cleanup-lifecycle latency regression; it was recorded through report_regression_fix.

Scenarios.Scenario: General configuration-variable parsing after moving the parser to the platform layer
Scenarios.CriticalPath: ConfigurationResolverExpression still scans serialized configuration and invokes the extracted parser at each candidate marker before interactive/non-interactive resolution. The parser body and advancement semantics are unchanged.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: CPU scales with serialized configuration length and variable structure exactly as before; the newly added standalone detector scans once backward in linear time and constant space.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Parsing is synchronous and local; the diff introduces no parallelism or queueing change.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache is used or invalidated by the extraction.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the removed method and added shared function are structurally equivalent, and the caller still advances to parsed.end + 1.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Serialized launch sizes vary, but there is no changed parser complexity on this path.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression; this is a behavior-preserving extraction plus a separately bounded detector.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 14 changed files and every diff page. No actionable diff-introduced performance issue met the reporting threshold. The review traced discovery, policy invalidation, variable-resolution retries, transport startup/teardown, cache retention, and pending-start cleanup; one concrete pre-existing indefinite-wait regression fixed by the PR was recorded for internal learning.
